status_summary: USAID, whose staff, missions and country strategies the text addresses, closed on 2025-07-01, and the executive record in the successor structure mostly runs the other way: CRS reported (2026-06-03) that a significant portion of congressionally directed religious freedom programs were terminated after the early 2025 aid pause, that the Office of International Religious Freedom moved back under the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, and that the ambassador-at-large nomination was returned to the President. The congressional element moved toward the text: the House committee summary of the FY2026 law (enacted 2026-02-03) says it increases support for religious freedom programs and restricts assistance to Nigeria until steps are taken to protect Christian communities, though no line specific to persecuted religious minorities was confirmed. Other steps are parallel: State's aid powers were delegated on 2025-08-21 to an Under Secretary whose title includes Religious Freedom, Nigeria was designated a Country of Particular Concern on 2025-10-31, a visa restriction policy for religious freedom violators was announced in December 2025, and State announced nearly $2 billion in health and humanitarian awards to faith-based organizations on 2026-08-06. No staff training or integration of religious freedom into all aid programs was found, so in_progress 25 is held at the bottom of the band on the appropriations element alone.

timeline.event: State published a delegation of foreign assistance powers to an Under Secretary whose title includes Religious Freedom; the text names no international religious freedom office.
The President announced Nigeria's designation as a Country of Particular Concern; CRS reported no resulting action had been announced.
An analysis republished by allAfrica noted that the President had threatened to cut aid to Nigeria and that past designations were seldom followed by sanctions.

Public Law 119-75 was enacted; the House Appropriations Committee's undated summary of the final State bill says it increases support for religious freedom programs and restricts assistance to Nigeria until measurable steps protect Christian communities.

CRS reported that a significant portion of programs using congressionally directed religious freedom funds were terminated after the 2025 aid pause (citing USCIRF), that the Office of International Religious Freedom returned to the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor in the 2025 reorganization, that the ambassador nomination was returned to the President, and that a visa restriction policy for religious freedom violators was announced in December 2025.

A report on a State release of 2026-08-06 described nearly $2 billion in health and humanitarian awards to faith-based organizations under the America First Global Health Strategy; the report does not mention religious freedom.

title: Make religious freedom central to development aid and fund persecuted minorities
uncertainties: The text of the FY2026 appropriations law was not read for religious freedom lines, so the House committee summary is the only basis and it gives no dollar figure; it prints no date and is dated here to the law's enactment (2026-02-03, per CRS). The Senate committee summary does not mention religious freedom. Whether any FY2026 line is specific to persecuted religious minorities was not confirmed. A search for training of State staff on religious freedom and development returned nothing. The 2025 Religious Liberty Commission is domestic and not counted. CRS does not mention Executive Order 13926, and no revocation of it was found; whether its $50 million budgeting target is met was not confirmed. Delegation No. 597 names religious freedom only in the Under Secretary's title and lists no religious freedom functions. The faith-based awards concern health and humanitarian delivery, a parallel step. The stage is a judgment call: the executive termination of programs and downgrading of the office run opposite to the text, which would support diverged, while the appropriations element moved toward it.
